messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall Sam: detected >30% packet loss to /24s announced by upstream-peer-3 in us-east-1. Auto-incident opened (INC-2026-045).
Sam (oncall): Got the page, looking. Anyone else seeing customer errors?
Marta (support): Tickets coming in for API timeouts and streaming disconnects. Multiple customers in us-east-1. Marking P2 for now but impact looks broad.
Kevin (SRE): I see elevated 5xx rates from frontends hitting model backends in us-east-1 and long tail latencies. Traces show TCP resets to 34.201.x.x ranges.
Anya (netops): BGP-looking issue from upstream-peer-3. Our BGP monitor shows repeated withdraws of our most-specifics and then a sudden nullroute announcement from the provider.
Sam (oncall): Paste the BGP dump and traceroutes?
Anya (netops): Traceroute from edge1 ->

```
traceroute to 34.201.12.0 (34.201.12.0), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.1.1  0.7 ms
 2  172.18.5.1  1.3 ms
 3  203.0.113.45  12.4 ms
 4  * * *
 5  * * *
```

Seems to drop right after provider hop. BGP table snippet:

```
> 203.0.113.0/24 (via 192.0.2.1) from upstream-peer-3  VALID
  Withdrawn: 203.0.113.0/24 -> community: no-export? then re-advertised as 203.0.113.0/24 -> next-hop 192.0.2.254 blackhole
```

Anya (netops): Provider claims they had a filter update that accidentally tagged our prefixes with a blackhole community. They say it's being reverted.
Alice (network-ops-lead): Contacted provider NOC on conference bridge; they're rolling back and verifying. ETA 10-15m.
Kevin (SRE): Workaround: we can failover traffic for affected customers to us-west region using our traffic-router policy, but that requires a canned config flip and will cause higher latency.
Sam (oncall): Let's prepare a targeted failover for critical customers only. Which customers are active in affected prefixes? Marta, can you list top 10 by requests now?
Marta (support): Pulling. Top impacted: AcmeCorp (prod), Healthly (prod), analytics-saas (staging). Sending CSV to #private-sec.
Sam (oncall): Ok. Kevin/Anya, what's the runbook for targeted BGP/edge policy failover?
Anya (netops): Steps:
1) Update traffic-router policy to add prefix-based override for AcmeCorp/Healthly to point at us-west-edge-2.
2) Trigger config push to edge fleet (rolling restart avoidance switch set).
3) Monitor BGP and app error rates.

Command snippet (dry run):

```
# dry-run: add override
traffic-router-cli add-override --prefix 34.201.12.0/24 --target us-west-edge-2 --reason "upstream-peer-3 blackhole"
traffic-router-cli push --dry-run
```

To apply, remove --dry-run.

Kevin (SRE): We should also enable application-level retry/backoff knob for SDK clients on a per-customer basis while we fail them over. Otherwise they'll see long tail errors.
Sam (oncall): I'm going to escalate to incident lead and call it P1 if provider rollback doesn't complete in 15m. Alice, keep the provider bridge open.
Alice (network-ops-lead): Bridge up: bridge.redwood.com/rooms/7082, provider NOC on. They're confirming rollback in progress.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to P1 by Sam (oncall) (auto-notify execs).

Anya (netops): Provider reports rollback applied at their edge at +5m. We see some announcements returning but still intermittent withdraws. BGP flap frequency has decreased but not stable.
Kevin (SRE): Starting targeted traffic-router override for AcmeCorp and Healthly now (applying).

```
traffic-router-cli push --apply
# output: override applied to 12/16 edges, 4 pending
```

Kevin (SRE): Pushed. Monitoring metrics: error rate for those customers dropped from 8% -> 0.6% within 60s.
Marta (support): Notifying customer success for AcmeCorp and Healthly with status guidance and recommended SDK retry patch. Drafting message.
Sam (oncall): Good. For remaining customers on those prefixes, either we leave them or we coordinate broader failover if provider doesn't stabilize.
Anya (netops): Provider NOC says they're doing a full control-plane audit; they expect full stability in ~30m. We're seeing fewer withdraws.
Alice (network-ops-lead): Can we add a temporary route prep: announce more-specifics via our backup transit to draw traffic away? That requires coordination with peering-policy and might trigger RPKI checks.
Kevin (SRE): I prefer using our traffic-router overrides rather than making more BGP noise. Safer.
Sam (oncall): Agreed. Do not announce new more-specifics without change board approval during an active incident.

incident-bot: Note added by Sam (oncall): "avoid more-specific announcements; use traffic-router overrides"

Marta (support): Customer success pinged. Draft status page update (staging): "We are investigating packet loss and routing instability affecting a subset of customers in us-east-1. Partial mitigations in place; targeted failovers completed for highest-impact customers. Working with upstream transit provider to resolve. Next update in 15 min." Anyone want to tweak?
Kevin (SRE): Add note about potential increased latency for affected customers due to failover.
Marta (support): Added. Publishing now.

Alice (network-ops-lead): Provider now reports full rollback at +18m and no withdraws for the last 10m. BGP tables look normal.
Anya (netops): Confirming convergence across our edge peers. No more blackhole community. Traceroutes are succeeding.
Kevin (SRE): Application metrics returning to baseline. Rolling back traffic-router overrides for the customers we failed over.

```
traffic-router-cli remove-override --prefix 34.201.12.0/24 --target us-west-edge-2
traffic-router-cli push --apply
```

Sam (oncall): Great. Let's keep incident open for 30m to validate stability. Assign postmortem to Alice + Anya to capture root cause and recommend vendor SLA/contract checks.
Alice (network-ops-lead): Taking postmortem. Will include timeline, BGP dumps, provider bridge logs, and customer impact table.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 marked as "monitoring" by Sam (oncall).

Marta (support): Final note to customers: "Routing instability from an upstream transit provider caused transient packet loss resulting in API timeouts. A subset of customers were temporarily failed over to alternate region; traffic has been restored and we're monitoring." Sent.

Sam (oncall): Thanks team. Follow-ups: (1) postmortem draft in 24h, (2) add automated detection to raise to P1 sooner if withdraw frequency > X in 10m, (3) vendor SLA review.
Kevin (SRE): Also recommend adding a runbook section for targeted traffic-router failover and automated telemetry to verify prefix blackhole via traceroute+bgp-snapshot.
Alice (network-ops-lead): Will include runbook changes. Closing channel updates; will ping when postmortem draft ready. :white_check_mark:
